solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bottom pinched by swimmer, dowdy

indicators.note: something pinched by another is gripped between its parts, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a fish is the archetypal swimmer
the rump is the bottom or backside

explanation.surface: Someone's backside gets nipped by a fellow bather, and that person is frumpily dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone drab, old-fashioned and unattractive in dress.

clue.text: More than ample babe regularly appearing in strip

indicators.note: the picked letters show up inside the other word, a container signal

parts.note: to flay is to strip the skin off

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word babe, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A generously built young woman shows up in a strip show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes B and B from babe, which go inside FLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh that is more than ample is soft and excessive, which is what flabby describes.

clue.text: Story yet to be read is thus beyond description?

definitions.meaning: a tale not yet told to anyone is still unrecounted
too great or vast to be expressed in words

explanation.walkthrough: 'is thus' joins the two senses; the first is a playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both not yet recounted and too great to be put into words.

clue.text: Suppose letters must include the ninth of them?

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, a container signal

parts.note: letters delivered by mail are the post
I is the ninth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether a sequence of letters has to contain the ninth one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points back to letters in the alphabet sense, though POST reads letters as mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as an assumption, the same as supposing.

clue.text: Oath required to spread article that's unfinished

parts.note: to strew is to scatter or spread about

indicators.note: the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone swears because they must spread out an incomplete item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts THE to TH. Strewth is a mild British and Australian exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, a contracted form of an oath sworn on God's truth.

clue.text: Good to punch boss, as moronic

indicators.note: a punch makes a hole, so one piece goes through the middle of another

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised ornamental knob
pi is short for pious, crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: Thumping your employer is described as a foolish thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like an employer but is the knob on a shield or belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both mean lacking intelligence or sense.

clue.text: The right people portray reforms in extremes of tyranny

indicators.note: the letters of portray are formed again in a new order
the first and last letters of tyranny

explanation.surface: A political picture of someone depicting reforms carried out under the harshest tyranny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges PORTRAY into TORYPAR; 'extremes of' tyranny gives TY. The Tory Party is the British Conservative Party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: The Conservatives are the main party of the political right in Britain, hence right-wing people.

clue.text: Top stop?

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, such as a jumper
a driver halts at the roadside

explanation.walkthrough: A pullover is a jumper (British for a sweater); to pull over is to stop the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper worn on the upper body; also a phrase for drawing a vehicle to the side of the road.

clue.text: Rehearsal — game over for Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: rummy is a card game
something over is done, finished

explanation.surface: A card game finished, said in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial sounds of RUMMY DONE gives DUMMY RUN, with the sound of DONE spelt RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run carried out before the real thing is a practice, just like a rehearsal.

clue.text: Playing sitar, go for creativity

indicators.note: the letters of sitar are played about with into a new order

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Have a go at playing the sitar to show some creativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges SITAR into ARTIS, followed by TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Athlete back on prozac at first, for preparatory examination

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
only the opening letter of prozac is used
the athlete's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a miler is a runner who races over a mile

explanation.surface: A runner who has gone back on the antidepressant is about to sit a preliminary exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athlete' suggests a sprinter, but a miler, a middle-distance runner, is needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for preliminary, a prelim is an exam taken before the main one.

clue.text: Mouth bit pulled up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is drawn upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A portion of a horse's mouthpiece is drawn upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns PART into TRAP; trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is informal slang for the mouth.

clue.text: One roaring round town primarily to see campanile

indicators.note: one word goes around another, a container signal

parts.note: a bellower is someone who roars

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of town is taken

explanation.surface: Someone shouting all around the town's centre goes to look at the bell tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives T from town, which sits inside BELLOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanile is the Italian word for a freestanding tower that holds bells.

clue.text: Setter finally invested in lousy agent

indicators.note: putting money into something places it inside, a container signal

parts.note: poxy is British slang for rubbish or lousy

indicators.note: the last letter of setter

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler has finally put money into a poor representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from Setter, which goes inside POXY, British slang for worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is someone authorised to act for another, as an agent does.

clue.text: Little fellow scratching head — because of this?

definitions.text: Little fellow scratching head — because of this?

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter

parts.note: titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: A small boy scratches his head, and the question is why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching head' removes the T from TITCH; read whole, an itch is why the little fellow is scratching his head.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritation of the skin is exactly what makes someone scratch.

clue.text: Actor reading a script, ultimately perplexed

indicators.note: the last letter of script
the letters of reading a are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer, reading a script, ends up baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T from script, and 'perplexed' rearranges READINGA and that T together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Upstart with average beauty detailed

parts.note: par is the average or normal level

indicators.note: de-tailed, with the tail or last letter removed

parts.note: Venus, goddess of love, stands for a great beauty

explanation.surface: A social climber who is ordinary to look at, with a meticulous description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, cutting VENUS to VENU.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a newcomer to wealth or status, an upstart.

clue.text: Scholar of no importance

definitions.meaning: of theoretical interest only, with no practical bearing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a university scholar and also something purely theoretical and irrelevant.

clue.text: Break loveless dullard, heartbroken?

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, O, and it is taken away

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person

indicators.note: the letters of heart are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a dull person without love has a broken heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' removes O (love, a zero) from BORE to leave BRE; 'broken' rearranges HEART into ATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rest from effort is a break or pause.

clue.text: Spaces here in Noah's aquarium?

parts.note: parking spaces are found here, and an ark full of carp would be Noah's fish tank

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as CARP ARK, a boat of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with marked bays for leaving vehicles; read as two words, an ark for fish.

clue.text: A thrill to put the boot in?

definitions.meaning: to strike with the foot, literally putting the boot in

explanation.walkthrough: To put the boot in is British for to attack someone viciously; here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a buzz of excitement and a blow with the foot.

clue.text: Artist unknown in part of India

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An unidentified painter is somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: Francisco Goya was a Spanish painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Goya, the Spanish painter of the late eighteenth century, is a celebrated artist.

clue.text: Catholic officer

definitions.meaning: with a small c, catholic means universal or wide-ranging

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' carries a capital to suggest the Church, but small-c catholic means all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: General means universal, the original sense of catholic, and is also a high military rank.

clue.text: Head of Christian Church involved in story? I've heard it all before!

indicators.note: the first letter of Christian
one piece is wrapped up inside another

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

explanation.surface: A church leader caught up in a tale, met with a weary response.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole exclamation, which is what one says on hearing a worn-out phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is a phrase so overused that hearing it again prompts that weary remark.

clue.text: Temperature in neither liquid nor gas, cool

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the third state of matter is solid

explanation.surface: A science lesson on temperature in matter that is in none of the fluid states, kept cold.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SOLID. 'cool' here means unemotional rather than cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and unexcitable, a sense of cool.

clue.text: Duck introduction to debt collector

indicators.note: the opening letter of debt

parts.note: a rake gathers up leaves

explanation.surface: A water bird is presented to someone who chases unpaid bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'debt collector' reads as one phrase, but the rake is a garden tool that collects leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple example relation: the male of the mallard and other ducks is called by this name.

clue.text: Romantic lad going out with client

indicators.note: the letters of lad and client are taken out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man is dating one of his customers, which is rather romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' looks like dating but rearranges LAD and CLIENT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner by the light of candles is the stock image of a romantic setting.

clue.text: Greatly enjoy winning motor race by some distance?

definitions.text: winning motor race by some distance?
definitions.meaning: a car finishing a whole circuit ahead of the rest

explanation.walkthrough: To be a lap up is to lead by one complete circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to relish eagerly, and literally describes being a full circuit ahead.

clue.text: Second musical yarn

parts.note: a mo is a moment or short time, a second
Hair is the 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: Another show tune, or the second story about a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story but means wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is yarn made from the hair of the Angora goat.

clue.text: Hot April, October briefly changeable

indicators.note: the letters can be changed into a new order

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October

explanation.surface: The weather in spring and autumn is hot and unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changeable' rearranges APRIL and OCT together.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hottest regions of the earth, so tropical means very hot.

clue.text: Something painful afoot about orchestra leader with a trumpet

indicators.note: one piece goes around another

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

indicators.note: the first letter of orchestra

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sore foot troubles the lead violinist, who has a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: CORN goes around O, then A. 'trumpet' is the trumpet-shaped centre of a daffodil, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the corona is the trumpet-like central part of a daffodil flower.

clue.text: S for Savalas?

parts.note: S is the head of the name Savalas, and the actor Telly Savalas was famously bald

explanation.walkthrough: S is the head of Savalas, and the bald actor Telly Savalas, who played TV detective Kojak, is the classic slaphead.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphead is British slang for a bald man, and Telly Savalas, who played Kojak, was bald.
